title: Ecosystems and Interdependence
summary: Biotic and abiotic factors, food chains and webs, energy pyramids, feeding relationships, adaptations and how humans affect the balance of an ecosystem.

notes.text: All the living organisms in an area together with the non-living parts of their environment, and the ways they interact.

notes.caption: The two parts of every ecosystem

items: **Habitat**: the place where an organism lives (e.g. a frog in a vlei).
**Population**: all the organisms of one species living in an area.
**Community**: all the populations of different species living in an area.
**Biome**: a large region with a similar climate and vegetation, such as the savanna, fynbos, grassland or Karoo.

rows: Makes its own food by photosynthesis
Breaks down dead material and waste, returning nutrients to the soil
Eats animals that are already dead

notes.text:
A **food chain** shows how energy passes from one organism to the next. The arrow points in the direction energy flows, meaning *is eaten by*.

grass → grasshopper → frog → snake → eagle
In a real ecosystem most animals eat more than one kind of food, so food chains link to form a **food web**. If one population changes, the whole web is affected.

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: Always draw arrows from the food to the feeder (from what is eaten to what eats it). Arrows show the flow of energy, not who hunts whom.

Each step in a food chain is a **trophic level**. Only about **10%** of the energy at one level passes to the next; the rest is used for life processes or lost as heat. This is why there are many producers, fewer herbivores and very few top carnivores.

notes.title: Energy along a food chain
notes.problem: The grass in a field stores 10 000 kJ of energy. About how much energy reaches the snake in the chain grass → grasshopper → frog → snake?

rows: One animal hunts and eats another
Organisms need the same limited resource
Lions and hyenas competing for prey
One benefits, the host is harmed
One benefits, the other is not affected

notes.text: An **adaptation** is a feature that helps an organism survive in its habitat, for example a camel's hump, a cactus's spines and thick waxy stem, or the long neck of a giraffe. Ecosystems stay in balance when populations are kept in check by food supply, predators and disease.

items: **Habitat destruction**: farming, mining and building remove homes for plants and animals.
**Pollution**: litter, sewage and pesticides poison organisms.
**Alien invasive species**: plants such as Port Jackson willow use large amounts of water and crowd out indigenous plants.
**Poaching and overfishing**: remove species faster than they can reproduce.

questions.prompt: Which of these is an ABIOTIC factor?
What is the name for an organism that makes its own food?
In a food chain, the arrow points from the organism that is eaten to the organism that eats it.
questions.explanation: Arrows show the direction in which energy flows.

questions.prompt: Match each organism to its role.
Plants in a food chain store 50 000 kJ of energy. Using the 10% rule, how much energy is passed on to the herbivores?
Oxpeckers eat ticks off a buffalo's back. What kind of relationship is this?
questions.explanation: The bird gets food and the buffalo loses its ticks, so both benefit.

questions.prompt: What term describes all the organisms of one species living in an area?
Explain why there are usually fewer lions than zebras in a game reserve.
questions.memo:
✓ Only about 10% of energy passes from one trophic level to the next (energy is lost as heat and used for life processes) (1)
✓ So there is much less energy available at the top of the food chain, which can support only a few carnivores (1)

questions.prompt: In the food chain grass → grasshopper → frog → snake, farmers spray pesticide that kills most of the grasshoppers. Describe what will happen to the grass and the frogs, and explain why.
questions.memo:
✓ The grass will increase because fewer grasshoppers eat it (1)
✓ The frog population will decrease (1)
✓ because they have less food (1)

questions.prompt: Explain how alien invasive plants threaten South African ecosystems.
questions.memo:
✓ They use large amounts of water / spread quickly (1)
✓ and crowd out indigenous plants, so the animals that depend on those plants lose food and shelter (1)
